CHOICE INTERNATIONAL Q2 FY27: RECORD REVENUE UP 33% YOY; ₹900 CR STRATEGIC INVESTMENT, 1:1 BONUS ISSUE & ₹710 CR ADVISORY ORDER BOOK

• Bonus Issue: Board recommended 1:1 bonus shares, subject to shareholder approval

• ₹900 Cr Strategic Investment: Choice Equity Broking received ₹900 Cr from South Korea's NH Investment & Securities after quarter-end, primarily to expand its Margin Trading Facility (MTF) business

• Broking Expansion: Demat accounts increased 14% YoY to 13.78 lakh, with 1.73 lakh accounts added during the quarter

• MTF Business: MTF loan book reached ₹463 Cr, while client assets under custody stood at ₹66,300 Cr

• Wealth Management: Total AUM reached ₹6,047 Cr, including ₹4,108 Cr mutual fund AUM and ₹291 Cr PMS and AIF AUM

• Equity AUM Growth: Mutual fund equity AUM increased 49% YoY to ₹3,013 Cr, while PMS and AIF AUM surged 127% YoY

• Government Advisory Order Book: Order book stood at ₹710 Cr, providing future execution and revenue visibility

• Investment Banking Pipeline: Holds 24 IPO mandates with estimated fundraising potential of ₹6,210 Cr; completed five IPOs raising approximately ₹680 Cr during Q2

• Feedback Infra Acquisition: Proposed acquisition received Committee of Creditors approval, with completion awaiting NCLT approval and other requirements

• NBFC Expansion: Loan book reached ₹935 Cr, with management focused on expanding retail lending while maintaining disciplined underwriting

• Asset Management Expansion: Launched its first actively managed mutual fund scheme, Choice Large & Mid Cap Fund, with plans to introduce additional investment products

• Wealth Distribution Growth: Structured and fixed-income product distribution reached ₹1,636 Cr during H1 FY27 versus ₹512 Cr YoY

• Insurance Business: Sold 75,173 policies and generated ₹81 Cr premium during Q2 FY27

• Future Growth Plans: Focused on scaling MTF lending, institutional broking, wealth management, asset management, government advisory and investment banking

DCW : STARTS RS 40 CR OPEN MARKET BUYBACK AT UP TO ₹58/SHARE

• Board on October 29, 2026 approved buyback of fully paid equity shares of face value ₹2 each via open market through BSE and NSE
• Maximum buyback size ₹40 Cr, maximum buyback price ₹58 per share, payable in cash
• Indicative maximum of 68,96,551 shares, equal to 4.53% of total paid-up equity capital and free reserves
• Buyback opens November 3, 2026; closing date earlier of February 8, 2027, full deployment of ₹40 Cr, or early closure with notice
• Offer is not open to promoters, promoter group and persons in control; physical shareholders must dematerialise to participate
• Uniform price not paid to all shareholders; price depends on last traded price with or without +/-1% deviation at time of bids
Impact: Positive (₹40 Cr open market buyback at up to ₹58/share for 4.53% of capital and free reserves is a cash return to non-promoter shareholders)

reports.text:
GNFC Q2 FY27: REVENUE UP 41% YOY; 50 KTPA AMMONIA, 200 KTPA NITRIC ACID & 163 KTPA AMMONIUM NITRATE EXPANSIONS UNDER EXECUTION

• Profitability: PBT increased 4.8% YoY but declined 42.1% QoQ to ₹241 Cr, impacted by lower chemical realisations and higher fixed costs

• Ammonia Expansion: 50 KTPA capacity expansion underway at Bharuch, aimed at improving ammonia plant reliability and reducing energy costs

• Weak Nitric Acid Expansion: 200 KTPA WNA-III project under execution at Bharuch, expected to strengthen market share and increase revenue

• Ammonium Nitrate Expansion: 163 KTPA AN-II project under execution at Bharuch, supporting higher production capacity and future profitability

• New Steam Boiler: Developing a 180–200 MT/hour CFBC steam boiler at Bharuch to improve operational reliability and reduce energy costs

• Expansion Timeline: Ammonia, WNA-III and AN-II projects are scheduled within FY27 execution plans, while the CFBC boiler execution schedule extends into FY29

• Bisphenol-A Expansion: Considering a 150 KTPA BPA manufacturing facility at Dahej, with a proposed execution window spanning FY28–FY31

• Polyols Expansion: Evaluating a 100 KTPA Polyols manufacturing project at Dahej as part of future chemical portfolio expansion

• Acetic Acid Expansion: Considering a 350 KTPA Acetic Acid manufacturing facility at Bharuch, with the proposed schedule extending through FY31

• Captive Power Plant: Dahej coal-based captive power plant has started operations, resulting in lower operating costs; remaining project activities are nearing completion

• Chemical Business: Revenue increased 40.4% YoY and 4% QoQ to ₹1,631 Cr, while segment profit increased 12% YoY but declined 58.4% QoQ to ₹177 Cr

• Fertilizer Business: Revenue increased 43% YoY and 72.1% QoQ to ₹1,117 Cr, while segment loss narrowed to ₹38 Cr from ₹85 Cr QoQ

• Urea Energy Norms: Revised Neem Urea energy norms of 6.37 Gcal/MT versus 6.20 Gcal/MT are favourable for the company; revision of fixed-cost compensation remains under discussion with the government

• H1 Performance: Revenue increased 40.4% YoY to ₹5,011 Cr, while PAT surged 94.1% to ₹495 Cr; comparison benefited from the previous year's Bharuch maintenance shutdown

• Cash Position: Cash and bank balances/deposits increased to ₹1,805 Cr from ₹1,111 Cr in March 2026, while borrowings stood at ₹109 Cr

• Working Capital: H1 operating cash flow declined to ₹141 Cr from ₹314 Cr YoY, impacted by higher working capital requirements and elevated feed and fuel costs

• Capex Progress: Capital work-in-progress stood at ₹781 Cr, mainly comprising WNA-III, Ammonium Nitrate-II and urea reactor replacement projects

• Future Growth Plans: Focused on expanding chemical manufacturing capacity, reducing energy costs, strengthening market share and evaluating new downstream chemical projects

• FY27 Guidance & Capex: Management explicitly stated that it does not provide forecasts or future earnings guidance.

MOTHERSON : PARTNERS WITH NTU SINGAPORE TO ADVANCE SPINHEAT TECHNOLOGY

• Collaboration is between NTU Singapore and MSSL (S) Pte Ltd, a Singapore-based subsidiary of Samvardhana Motherson International
• Spinheat is a magnetic induction technology that can cure industrial coatings in minutes using significantly less energy than conventional oven-based methods
• Technology uses magnetic nanoparticles embedded in adhesives and resins; an alternating magnetic field generates heat directly within the coating, avoiding heating the entire component
• Early lab results show bonding strength of conventional 24-hour oven curing achieved in about an hour, with potential to cut energy use and CO2 emissions
• Aim is to industrialise the technology for real-world production, including resin coatings across automotive and aerospace components
• No financial or deal value disclosed in the release
Impact: Positive (Early-stage R&D tie-up adds material-science capability for faster, cleaner manufacturing, though no commercial or financial terms disclosed)

E2E : LAUNCHES BLAZE PAY-PER-TOKEN AI INFERENCE SERVICE

• Blaze is a pay-per-token inference service for open AI models, launched globally on 02-11-2026
• Offers a single OpenAI-compatible API for models including NVIDIA Nemotron, Sarvam, DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM and Gemma
• Built on NVIDIA DSX OS with NVIDIA Dynamo serving and CUDA kernels; runs on NVIDIA GPU infrastructure hosted in India
• Targets latency-sensitive use cases such as voice, coding agents, document AI, image and video generation
• Works with E2E's TIR platform, giving labs and enterprises an India-hosted path from training to production inference
• AI factory capacity expanding to about 14.6 MW, including a 1,024-GPU NVIDIA Blackwell cluster live since May 2026 and additional 5.4 MW of Blackwell capacity
Impact: Positive (Monetises India-hosted sovereign AI factory capacity as production inference revenue, strengthening the E2E Cloud platform offering)

EKI ENERGY : SEBI IMPOSES RS 88 L PENALTY, 2-MONTH MARKET BAN

• Order dated October 30, 2026 from SEBI received on November 2, 2026; total penalties at ₹88 L on company and individuals.
• Company restrained from accessing securities market and dealing in securities for 2 months; penalty of ₹12 L payable within 45 days.
• Company penalty split as ₹7 L under Section 15HA and ₹5 L under Section 15HB.
• Individuals restrained for 1-12 months, with penalties including ₹28 L on Manish Kumar Dabkara and ₹19 L on Mohit Kumar Agarwal.
• EKI does not concur with certain assertions; evaluating legal remedies including appeal before SAT under Section 15T.
• Company says no other material impact on financial, operational or other activities; business and ongoing projects remain functional.
Impact: Negative (Regulatory penalty and two-month market ban create overhang; proposed appeal may extend uncertainty).

MARICO Q2 FY27: TARGETS ₹15,000+ CR FY27 REVENUE & MID-20% EBITDA GROWTH; ₹20,000+ CR REVENUE VISION BY FY30, PAT UP 31% YOY

• FY27 Revenue Guidance: Management expects teens revenue growth and consolidated revenue exceeding ₹15,000 Cr during FY27

• FY27 EBITDA Guidance: Targets mid-twenties EBITDA growth, supported by volume expansion, improving product mix and operating leverage

• FY27 Volume Guidance: Expects double-digit domestic volume growth and mid-teens constant currency growth in international business

• FY30 Revenue Target: Management aims to achieve ₹20,000+ Cr consolidated revenue by FY30, with double-digit revenue CAGR

• FY30 EBITDA Target: Aspires to deliver mid-teens EBITDA CAGR, supported by premiumisation and profitable scaling of new businesses

• Margin Performance: EBITDA margin expanded to 18.2% from 16.2% YoY but declined from 20.7% QoQ, while gross margin improved approximately 600 bps YoY

• Domestic Business: Revenue increased 10% YoY to ₹2,916 Cr, supported by 10% underlying volume growth and broad-based market share gains

• Parachute Coconut Oil: Volumes surged 13% YoY, highest growth in 22 quarters, while market share increased to 60%

• Value-Added Hair Oils: Revenue grew 21% YoY, with market share increasing 80 bps, supported by premiumisation and distribution expansion

• Foods Business: Revenue surged 45% YoY, crossing ₹1,500 Cr annualised revenue run-rate, supported by Saffola Foods and acquired brands

• Premium Personal Care: Annualised revenue run-rate crossed ₹500 Cr, while digital-first businesses reached approximately ₹1,150 Cr

• FY27 Digital Business Target: Expects digital-first premium personal care businesses to achieve double-digit EBITDA margin by FY27-end, expanding to teens in the medium term

• Premium Portfolio Expansion: Targets Foods and Premium Personal Care contribution of approximately 27% of India revenue by FY27-end and 33% by FY30

• FY30 Portfolio Strategy: Aims to increase premium and digital categories to 50% of the overall portfolio from 37% in FY26

• International Business: Revenue increased 23% YoY in INR terms, with constant currency growth of 13%; Vietnam grew 22%, MENA 15%, South Africa 15% and Bangladesh 5%

• International Expansion: Targets 20%+ revenue CAGR in international markets excluding Bangladesh, with premium categories contributing approximately 40% of international revenue by FY30

• Distribution Expansion: Project SETU 2.0 will focus on AI-enabled selling, deeper rural penetration and expansion of Foods and Premium Personal Care across general trade

• Distribution Targets: Direct distribution reach scaled to over 1.5x FY24 levels, while rural stockist penetration increased approximately 2x by the FY27 exit target

• H1 Performance: Revenue increased 18% YoY to ₹7,854 Cr, EBITDA grew 26% to ₹1,528 Cr and PAT increased 28% to ₹1,180 Cr

• Cost Management: Softer copra prices and the MarVal cost optimisation programme expected to support profitability, although crude-linked and vegetable oil inflation remain risks

• Future Growth Plans: Focused on core brand growth, premiumisation, scaling digital-first brands, international expansion, AI-driven distribution and improving profitability

- 𝗥𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗻𝘂𝗲: Increased by 16% YoY to ₹2,145 million from ₹1,845 million in Q2 FY26. Sequentially, revenue grew 12% QoQ from ₹1,917 million in Q1 FY27.
- 𝗘𝗕𝗜𝗧𝗗𝗔: Grew 20% YoY to ₹721 million (vs. ₹601 million in Q2 FY26), marking a 36% increase QoQ from ₹529 million in Q1 FY27.
- 𝗣𝗔𝗧: Rose 14% YoY to ₹512 million (vs. ₹447 million in Q2 FY26), with a significant 33% QoQ jump from ₹386 million in Q1 FY27.
- 𝗠𝗮𝗿𝗴𝗶𝗻𝘀: EBITDA margin stood at 34% & PAT margin at 24% for Q2 FY27.

𝗛1 𝗙𝗬27 𝗣𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲 (𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘀𝗼𝗹𝗶𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗱):

- 𝗘𝗕𝗜𝗧𝗗𝗔: Increased 7% YoY to ₹1,250 million from ₹1,165 million in H1 FY26.
- 𝗣𝗔𝗧: Saw a 5% uptick YoY to ₹897 million from ₹852 million in H1 FY26.
- 𝗠𝗮𝗿𝗴𝗶𝗻𝘀: EBITDA margin was 31% & PAT margin was 22% for H1 FY27.

𝗦𝗲𝗴𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗣𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲:

- 𝗛𝘂𝗺𝗮𝗻 𝗡𝘂𝘁𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: Contributed ~60% of revenue. Grew 6% YoY in Q2 FY27 to ₹1,285 million & 11% QoQ. H1 FY27 remained flat YoY at ₹2,443 million.
- 𝗔𝗻𝗶𝗺𝗮𝗹 𝗡𝘂𝘁𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: Contributed ~12% of revenue. Showed strong growth of 37% YoY in Q2 FY27 to ₹265 million & 5% QoQ. H1 FY27 grew 14% YoY to ₹517 million.
- 𝗜𝗻𝗱𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝗕𝗶𝗼-𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗰𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗴: Contributed 17% of revenue. Grew 43% YoY in Q2 FY27 to ₹365 million & 19% QoQ. Food business within this segment grew 48% YoY. H1 FY27 grew 37% YoY to ₹671 million.
- 𝗦𝗽𝗲𝗰𝗶𝗮𝗹𝗶𝘇𝗲𝗱 𝗠𝗮𝗻𝘂𝗳𝗮𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴: Contributed 11% of revenue. Outperformed with 25% YoY growth in Q2 FY27 to ₹231 million & 15% QoQ. H1 FY27 grew 32% YoY to ₹431 million.

- 𝗘𝘂𝗿𝗼𝗽𝗲: Contributed 5% of Q2 FY27 revenue, down 10% YoY. H1 FY27 revenue was ₹236 million (+14% YoY).

- 𝗥𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗹𝗱: Contributed 3% of Q2 FY27 revenue, growing 54% YoY. H1 FY27 revenue was ₹122 million (+54% YoY).

🔹 FY30 – International Opportunities: Evaluate overseas markets, subject to feasibility, while maintaining disciplined expansion.

MSafe Equipments

Revenue up 54%. Profit jumps 55%! 🚀

Strong Q2 FY27 performance with double-digit growth across key financials!

📈 Revenue: Rs. 40.4 Cr
↑ 53.6% YoY | ↑ 27.0% QoQ
📈 EBITDA: Rs. 15.6 Cr
↑ 49.6% YoY | ↑ 23.6% QoQ
📈 PAT: Rs. 8.49 Cr
↑ 55.4% YoY | ↑ 16.7% QoQ

Strong growth momentum on both a yearly and quarterly basis!

**JEFFERIES ON INDIGO**

Target: ₹5,650
Earlier Target: ₹5,840
Recommendation: Buy

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Guides for low-single-digit ASK growth in FY27 and mid-teens capacity expansion in FY28
- Expects 25%+ PRASK growth in Q3, supported by disciplined capacity deployment
- Cuts FY27 EPS estimates by 9%; elevated fuel costs remain key earnings risk

**JEFFERIES ON INDIA STRATEGY**

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Q2 mid-quarter review indicates upgrades holding up
- Results remain healthy, with upgrade ratio sustaining above 50%
- Banks, 2Ws, Power Utilities and consumer tech delivered well
- IT and staples remain mixed; 4Ws weak
- Management commentary indicates pockets of festive demand strength
- MSCI India FY27 earnings growth expectations upgraded 1 percentage point to 15%

**INVESTEC ON ACC & AMBUJA CEMENTS**

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Maintains Buy on Ambuja Cement, TP Rs 615; Hold on ACC, TP Rs 1,683
- Ambuja announces 29.7 MT grinding and 10.3 MT clinker capacity expansion at Rs 154 bn capex
- Targets cement capacity of 149 MT by FY29 and 155 MT by FY30; expects H2 volume growth ahead of industry
- Captive fly ash and fiscal incentives offer cost advantages; execution and cost guidance remain key concerns

**MORGAN STANLEY ON COAL INDIA**

Target: ₹480
Recommendation: Overweight

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Strong thermal power demand and five-year-low coal inventories support an earnings upgrade cycle
- Elevated global coal prices could drive higher e-auction premiums and realisations
- Expects sustained demand recovery, supported by low power-plant coal stocks and rising international prices

**UBS ON INDIGO**

Target: ₹5,050
Earlier Target: ₹5,450
Recommendation: Neutral

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Guides for low-single-digit ASK growth in FY27 and 25%+ PRASK growth in Q3
- Targets ~300 bn ASKs by FY30, supported by international expansion and long-haul operations
- Cuts FY27/FY28 EBITDA estimates by 7%/20%; raises FY29 estimates by 6% on fuel-cost normalisation

**NOMURA ON INDIGO**

Target: ₹6,200
Earlier Target: ₹6,000
Recommendation: Neutral

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Expects 30% PRASK growth in Q3, with pricing recovering 80–90% of fuel-cost inflation
- Forecasts FY28 EBITDA margin expansion to 21%, supported by lower fuel prices and fleet growth
- Raises FY27/FY28 EBITDA estimates by 11%/3%; expects 40% EBITDA CAGR over FY26–29

**HSBC ON INDIGO**

Target: ₹5,545
Recommendation: Buy

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Guides for 25%+ PRASK growth and low-single-digit capacity expansion in FY27
- Expects ex-fuel unit costs to rise high-single to low-double digits; international capacity growth to moderate
- Ancillary, cargo, business class and BluChip loyalty programme remain growth priorities; targets mid-teens capacity growth in FY28

**HSBC ON ASIAN PAINTS**

Target: ₹2,420
Earlier Target: ₹2,650
Recommendation: Hold

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Retains FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 18–20%; rising input costs and competition threaten recovery
- Premiumisation and festive demand offer support, but dealer promotions and consumer downgrading remain risks
- Cuts target valuation multiple to 40x from 45x; questions potential savings from backward integration

**GOLDMAN SACHS ON CRAFTSMAN AUTOMATION**

Target: ₹13,000
Recommendation: Buy

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Q2 revenue/EBITDA/net profit grow 47%/30%/68% YoY; results broadly in line
- EBITDA margin contracts 178 bps YoY to 13.3% amid input-cost pressures
- New production launches, higher-CC engine mix and Sunbeam margin recovery to support H2 growth
- Cuts FY27–29 EPS estimates by 2% each; expects stronger growth from Tata Motors-Stellantis partnership

**KOTAK ON LAURUS LABS**

Target: ₹1,400
Recommendation: Sell

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Expects ~34% EBITDA CAGR over FY26–29, with margins reaching ~36% by FY29
- Plans Rs 30 bn-plus capex over FY27–28, largely targeting high-growth projects
- Peptides, oligonucleotides and advanced therapies expand CDMO opportunities; valuations remain a concern

**GOLDMAN SACHS ON PIDILITE INDUSTRIES**

Target: ₹1,700
Earlier Target: ₹1,850
Recommendation: Buy

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Q2 revenue rises 20.9% YoY; EBITDA grows 3.1%, missing estimates by 6.4%
- Underlying volume growth at 10.7%; gross margin contracts 650 bps YoY on higher input costs
- Additional 3–5% price hikes and easing VAM prices expected to support H2 margin recovery
- Cuts FY27–29 EPS estimates by 1–1.7%; expects FY27 EBITDA margin at higher end of 20–24% guidance

**KOTAK ON RR KABEL**

Target: ₹2,000
Earlier Target: ₹1,900
Recommendation: Sell

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Cuts FY27 W&C volume growth guidance to 14–15% from 18% earlier
- Retains FY27 W&C EBIT margin guidance at 9.5%; targets FMEG operating breakeven
- Raises FY27–29 earnings estimates by 7–9%; flags intensifying competition

**KOTAK ON HEXAWARE TECHNOLOGIES**

Target: ₹620
Earlier Target: ₹660
Recommendation: Buy

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Withdraws CY26 revenue growth guidance; expects sequential revenue decline in Q4
- Cuts CY27–28 EPS estimates by 6.5–7%; lowers EBIT margin guidance to 13–13.5%
- New CEO expected to focus on large-deal conversion, sales execution and margin improvement

**JEFFERIES ON RAYMOND LIFESTYLE**

Target: ₹800
Earlier Target: ₹900
Recommendation: Buy

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Q2 revenue grows 13% YoY; EBITDA declines 3% as margin contracts 173 bps to 10.6%
- Branded Apparel revenue rises 20%; Garmenting revenue/EBITDA jump 26%/75% YoY
- Festive and wedding demand, strong garmenting orders and store rationalisation to drive H2 recovery
- Expects FY26–29 revenue/EBITDA/PAT CAGR of 9%/14%/23%; retains FY27 double-digit revenue growth guidance

**KOTAK ON IT SECTOR – COGNIZANT**

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Maintains Neutral sector view; Cognizant cuts CY26 revenue growth guidance to 4–4.4%
- Weaker discretionary spending in healthcare and consumer verticals clouds demand recovery
- CY26 adjusted EBIT margin guidance narrowed to 16.1%; EPS growth guidance retained at 8–10%
- Flags uncertainty around CY27 acceleration amid weaker deal conversion and client spending

**UBS ON SUZLON ENERGY**

Target: ₹58
Earlier Target: ₹66
Recommendation: Buy

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Q2 revenue rises 26% YoY; EBITDA remains flat, with margin contracting 386 bps YoY to 14.8%
- Wind turbine deliveries grow 26% YoY to 710 MW; order book of ~6 GW provides 18-month visibility
- Cuts FY27 EBITDA margin guidance to 15–16% from 17%; H1 operating cash flow turns negative at Rs 2 bn
- Cuts FY27–29 EPS estimates by 10%/11%/9%; retains FY31 targets of ~40% market share and ~10 GW annual sales

**KOTAK ON ECLERX**

Target: ₹1,450
Recommendation: Sell

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Expects revenue growth to decelerate to high single digits in 2HFY27
- Weak deal wins and smaller AI-related contracts threaten double-digit growth sustainability
- Cuts FY28–29 EPS estimates by 5–6%; flags structural profitability pressures

**KOTAK ON ICRA**

Target: ₹6,400
Recommendation: Buy

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Expects ratings revenue CAGR of 14% over FY27–29, supported by corporate credit demand
- Forecasts ratings segment margin expansion to 43% by FY29
- Higher interest rates could moderate near-term growth; non-ratings acquisitions offer diversification

**GOLDMAN SACHS ON GODREJ CONSUMER**

Target: ₹1,030
Recommendation: Buy

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Q2 revenue rises 15.4% YoY; EBITDA grows 11.8%, margin at 18.6%
- India volumes grow 7%; home care sales rise 19% despite inventory correction
- Retains FY27 guidance of high-single-digit India volume growth and double-digit consolidated revenue/EBITDA growth

**JEFFERIES ON HEXAWARE TECHNOLOGIES**

Target: ₹470
Earlier Target: ₹500
Recommendation: Underperform

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Withdraws CY26 revenue growth guidance amid delayed large-deal ramp-ups
- Lowers CY26 EBIT margin guidance to 13–13.5%; expects wage hikes to pressure margins
- Forecasts ~5% organic revenue CAGR over CY25–28; cuts revenue/EPS estimates by 2–3%

**NOMURA ON ECLERX**

Target: ₹1,710
Earlier Target: ₹1,850
Recommendation: Neutral

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Q2 constant-currency revenue grows 1.4% QoQ; EBITDA margin falls 310 bps YoY to 23.9%
- Annual contract value declines 33% YoY to $30.8 mn amid weak deal wins
- Cuts FY27–28 EPS estimates by 7–8%; flags client budget pressures and longer decision cycles

**JEFFERIES ON TRENT**

Target: ₹3,300
Earlier Target: ₹3,435
Recommendation: Hold

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Retains annual store-opening guidance of 200–250 Zudio and 50 Westside stores
- Emerging categories, online channels and smaller-city expansion remain growth drivers
- Flags input-cost inflation and competitive pressures; lowers valuation multiples

**JEFFERIES ON ASIAN PAINTS**

Target: ₹3,025
Earlier Target: ₹3,350
Recommendation: Buy

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Expects 8–9% decorative volume growth in H2, aided by festive and wedding demand
- Retains FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 18–20%; additional price hikes to offset inflation
- VAM/VAE backward integration expected to deliver 3–5 percentage-point benefit at full potential

**KOTAK ON SCHAEFFLER INDIA**

Target: ₹3,800
Recommendation: Reduce

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Expects rising content per vehicle, e-mobility adoption and export expansion to drive growth
- Sees double-digit CAGR in bearings, industrial and aftermarket businesses over CY25–28
- Domestic auto demand and gradual raw-material cost pass-through expected to support earnings

Target: ₹220
Earlier Target: ₹215
Recommendation: Buy

- Expects FY27 revenue growth at upper end of 21–23.5% guidance
- UPI MDR monetisation expected to add Rs 1.3 bn to FY28 adjusted EBITDA
- Forecasts FY26–28 revenue/adjusted EBITDA CAGR of 23%/36%, aided by affordability and payments growth

**GOLDMAN SACHS ON ASIAN PAINTS**

Target: ₹2,375
Earlier Target: ₹2,725
Recommendation: Sell

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Q2 revenue rises 16.9% YoY; EBITDA grows just 3.6%, missing estimates by 11.6%
- Decorative volume growth slows to 6.4% from 9% in Q1; gross margin contracts 350 bps YoY
- Management retains FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 18–20%; expects H2 volume growth of 8–9%
- Cuts FY27–29 EPS estimates by around 2%; high input costs and competition to delay recovery

**CITI ON TRENT**

Target: ₹2,815
Earlier Target: ₹2,950
Recommendation: Sell

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Expects annual store-opening pace to remain broadly consistent, with expansion into smaller cities
- Raises FY27–29 revenue estimates by ~2% amid improving consumer sentiment
- Cuts FY27/28 EPS by 6%/3%; flags valuation concerns and risks from input-cost inflation

**BOFA SECURITIES ON WIRES & CABLES SECTOR**

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Retains 14% industry CAGR forecast over FY26–29 despite recent stock corrections
- Industry expected to grow from Rs 1.27 trillion in FY26 to Rs 1.9 trillion by FY29
- Stress-case analysis suggests 12–13% growth even under weaker demand assumptions
- Global electrification, power infrastructure and exports offer structural growth opportunities
- Prefers Polycab and KEI over Havells; cuts target prices by 14–24% on valuation reset

**JEFFERIES ON GODREJ CONSUMER**

Target: ₹1,075
Earlier Target: ₹1,400
Recommendation: Buy

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Q2 revenue grows ~19% YoY; EBITDA rises 13%, India volumes grow 7%
- Home care grows 19%; international business remains strong, led by Indonesia and GAUM
- Cuts FY27–28 EPS estimates by 3% amid rising input costs; retains double-digit growth guidance

**BOFA SECURITIES ON HAVELLS INDIA**

Target: ₹900
Earlier Target: ₹1,050
Recommendation: Underperform

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Stock corrects 19% since September; revised TP implies 11% downside
- Expects 16% EPS CAGR over FY26–29 versus historical 24% growth
- Higher wires exposure increases vulnerability to competitive pricing pressure
- Lloyd business overhang persists; valuations remain expensive despite correction

**NOMURA ON NBFCs**

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Prefers Piramal Finance, Tata Capital, Aadhar Housing Finance and Bajaj Finance
- Monsoon deficit of 13% and Rabi sowing decline of 37% YoY raise rural income concerns
- Flags drought, food inflation, higher interest rates and regulatory pressures as key risks
- Favours urban housing/business lenders over rural, vehicle and microfinance-focused NBFCs

**BOFA SECURITIES ON KEI INDUSTRIES**

Target: ₹4,800
Earlier Target: ₹6,300
Recommendation: Buy

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Stock corrects 33% since September; revised TP implies 23% upside
- Expects 20% EPS CAGR over FY26–29, supported by Sanand capacity ramp-up
- Exports, EHV cables and improving product mix to drive growth
- Competitive pressures manageable; remains preferred pick alongside Polycab

**MACQUARIE ON ASIAN PAINTS**

Target: ₹3,300
Recommendation: Outperform

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Q2 revenue grows 16.9% YoY; EBITDA rises just 3.6%, missing estimates
- Decorative volumes grow 6.4%; gross margin contracts ~400 bps YoY
- Retains 18–20% EBITDA margin guidance; expects pricing and backward integration to support recovery

**JEFFERIES ON COAL INDIA**

Target: ₹460
Earlier Target: ₹500
Recommendation: Buy

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Q2 cash EBITDA rises 29% YoY; PAT jumps 53%, dispatch volumes grow 12%
- Power plant coal inventories fall to six days against a 10-year average of 15 days
- Expects 7% EPS CAGR over FY26–29; dividend yield of ~7% supports total returns

**BOFA SECURITIES ON POLYCAB**

Target: ₹8,800
Earlier Target: ₹11,000
Recommendation: Buy

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Stock corrects 18% since September; valuations reset despite strong earnings outlook
- Expects 20% EPS CAGR over FY26–29; industry leadership and exports support growth
- Limited exposure to global AI capex; competition and commodity concerns seen as manageable
- Prefers Polycab for its 24% market share, strong margins and attractive valuations

**NOMURA ON APAR INDUSTRIES**

Target: ₹17,500
Earlier Target: ₹15,400
Recommendation: Buy

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Q2 revenue grows 21% YoY; EBITDA jumps 55%, beating estimates by 32%
- Cable order book reaches Rs 30 bn, supported by data-centre orders from Google and Amazon
- Raises FY27–29 EBITDA estimates by 5–10% on strong transformer oil profitability and conductor demand

**JEFFERIES ON LAURUS LABS**

Target: ₹2,100
Earlier Target: ₹1,700
Recommendation: Hold

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Q2 revenue rises 33% YoY; EBITDA jumps 86%, with margin expanding to 34%
- Peptide manufacturing capacity reaches 16,000 litres; commercial revenues expected from 2HFY28/FY29
- Raises FY27–28 EPS estimates by 6%/4%, supported by improved product mix and CDMO growth

**CITI ON INDIAN IT SERVICES**

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Remain cautious on Indian IT services despite Cognizant outperforming Indian peers in Q3CY26
- Cognizant revenue grows 4.8% YoY in constant currency versus 0.6–4.1% growth for Indian IT peers
- Elevated competition, AI-led productivity gains and market-share shifts towards GCCs remain key headwinds
- Indian IT valuations remain expensive; TCS/Infosys/HCL Tech trade at 16x/15x/18x forward PE versus Cognizant at 11x
- Demand remains challenging despite AI opportunities; sector's valuation premium to global peers limits upside

**BERNSTEIN ON TRENT**

Target: ₹3,500
Recommendation: Outperform

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Q2 standalone revenue grows 22% YoY; retail area expands 26%
- Gross margin improves 120 bps YoY to 44.5%, aided by premiumisation and product elevation
- Flags slower Zudio/Westside store additions and 3% decline in revenue productivity per sq. ft.

**GOLDMAN SACHS ON LAURUS LABS**

Target: ₹1,600
Earlier Target: ₹1,425
Recommendation: Sell

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Q2 revenue grows 33% YoY; EBITDA surges 86%, with margin at 34%

- CDMO revenue jumps ~86% YoY, supported by late-stage projects and commercial API supplies

- Raises FY27–29 EPS estimates by 17–22%, but flags expensive valuations at ~75x FY28 P/E

**NOMURA ON TCS**

Target: ₹2,630
Recommendation: Buy

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**

- AI revenue reaches $3.1 billion annualised, growing 15–20% sequentially

- Only 5% of enterprises ready to deploy advanced AI at scale, offering significant opportunity

- AI-led modernisation could shorten transformation timelines from 3–4 years to 6–18 months

- Expects deflationary pressures to ease; AI investments of $1 billion annually weigh on near-term margins

**HSBC ON RURAL INDIA**

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Rural demand remains steady, with most companies maintaining neutral to positive outlook

- 2026 driest year in five years; 44% of districts report deficient rainfall

- Reservoir levels 18% below 10-year average; South worst affected at 46% below average

- Higher crop prices support affluent farmers but pressure landless and lower-income households

- Rabi crop risks could weigh on rural consumption in H2FY27

**UBS ON BLUE STAR**

Target: ₹2,000
Recommendation: Buy

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Q2 revenue/EBITDA/PAT grow 21%/10%/2% YoY, beating consensus estimates
- Unitary Products revenue jumps 29%; profitability remains subdued at 2.3%
- Data-centre demand supports Rs 14 bn order inflows; expects stronger MEP orders ahead

Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now
